title: Understanding Dealing Ranges in Trading (Get Better Risk Reward)
description: Learn dealing ranges, premium, discount, EQ, fractal setups, and higher timeframe targets to improve entries and risk reward.

body.text: Introduction
A dealing range is the overall range you are trading within or toward.
Within the TTrades Fractal Model, the fractal gives you the setup. The dealing range gives you the range around that setup.
Find the swing point you are trading away from, find the higher timeframe swing that created it, and mark the range.
From there, use premium, discount, and EQ to position the trade and measure the available risk reward.
What Is A Dealing Range?
A dealing range is the range between the swing point you are trading away from and the higher timeframe swing you are trading toward.
For a bullish range, start with the low you are trading away from. Find the higher timeframe swing high that made that low and mark the range.
For a bearish range, start with the high you are trading away from. Find the higher timeframe swing low that made that high and mark the range.
That is the dealing range.
Finding A Bullish Dealing Range
Start with a valid fractal model.
If you have a Candle 2 closure and are looking to trade Candle 3 higher, start with the Candle 2 low.
Move to the higher timeframe and find the swing high that made that low.
It will not always be Candle 1. Keep moving through the higher timeframe until you find the swing high.
Mark the high to the low.
That is your bullish dealing range.
Finding A Bearish Dealing Range
The bearish range works the same way.
Start with a valid fractal model and find the high you are trading away from.
Move to the higher timeframe and find the swing low that made that high.
Mark the high to the low.
That is your bearish dealing range.
Premium, Discount, And EQ
Split the dealing range at 50%.
The upper half is premium.
The lower half is discount.
EQ sits in the middle.
For bullish setups, look for longs in discount or around EQ.
For bearish setups, look for shorts in premium or around EQ.
The goal is simple. Enter with enough range between the entry and the target to reach your risk reward.
Why Entry Position Matters
If you are long from discount, you have more range between your entry and the dealing range high.
If you are long from premium, you are already closer to the target.
The same applies to shorts.
A short in premium has more range toward the dealing range low. A short deep in discount is already closer to the target.
The setup can still work from a poor location. The issue is how much range is left for the trade.
Dealing Ranges Are Fractal
Dealing ranges can form on every timeframe.
You can have a daily dealing range, an hourly dealing range, and another dealing range on the 15 minute or 5 minute.
The process stays the same.
Find the swing point you are trading away from. Find the swing that created it. Mark the range. Then use premium, discount, and EQ.
Using Dealing Ranges To Avoid Poor Entries
A bearish setup deep in discount may still work, but the target is already close.
A bullish setup high in premium has the same problem.
Price can continue, but there may not be enough range for the risk reward you want.
The dealing range gives you a mechanical way to see how much room is left before entering.
Using The Dealing Range Target
The dealing range high is the target for a bullish range.
The dealing range low is the target for a bearish range.
Use that target to measure the available risk reward before entering.
Once the first target is taken, runners can continue toward the dealing range target.
Multiple Dealing Ranges
Multiple dealing ranges can overlap.
A lower timeframe setup can form inside a higher timeframe dealing range.
For example, a short can form in premium of both the 5 minute and higher timeframe dealing ranges.
Now the entry is positioned within both ranges.
The same process applies to bullish setups.
Putting It All Together
Start with the fractal model.
Find the swing point you are trading away from. Find the higher timeframe swing that created it. Mark the range.
Then split it at EQ.
Look for longs in discount or around EQ. Look for shorts in premium or around EQ.
Use the dealing range target to measure the available risk reward.
That is the dealing range.
Final Thoughts
The fractal model gives you the setup.
The dealing range gives you the range.
Use premium, discount, and EQ to position the trade.
Then use the dealing range target to measure the risk reward.
Keep it mechanical.
